summary: This screen is the profile settings page of a task management application called Nimbus, allowing users to update their personal details and notification preferences.

stack.name: React + Vite
stack.why: Provides a fast, reactive development environment suitable for interactive settings pages.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Enables rapid styling with utility classes matching the clean sidebar and card layout.

components.name: Sidebar
components.purpose: Displays app branding, navigation links, and user settings/logout options.

components.name: HeaderBar
components.purpose: Contains the global search input and user profile avatar.

components.name: SettingsTabs
components.purpose: Allows switching between Profile, Notifications, Billing, and Integrations views.

components.name: ProfileForm
components.purpose: Manages user input fields and toggle switches for profile settings.

steps.title: Set up project and base layout
steps.detail: Initialize a Vite + React project with Tailwind CSS. Create the main layout container with the dark sidebar and light content area.

steps.title: Build the sidebar navigation
steps.detail: Implement the Nimbus logo, menu items (Dashboard, Projects, My tasks, Reports, Team, Settings, Log out), and active state highlighting using React state or router.

steps.title: Build the header bar
steps.detail: Add the global search input ('Search projects and tasks...') and the 'AK' user avatar to the top right of the content area.

steps.title: Build the settings header and tabs
steps.detail: Create the 'Settings' title, subtitle paragraph, and the horizontal tab navigation (Profile, Notifications, Billing, Integrations).

steps.title: Build the profile form card
steps.detail: Create the white card container with inputs for Full name ('Asha Kapoor') and Work email ('asha@fernway.io'). Add toggle switches for email due dates and weekly sprint reports.

steps.title: Implement form actions and state
steps.detail: Wire up the 'Cancel' and 'Save changes' buttons to manage form state changes and trigger mock API save requests.

steps.title: Review responsiveness
steps.detail: Check that the sidebar collapses or adapts appropriately on smaller viewports and the settings card scales cleanly.

behaviour: Clicking sidebar navigation items updates the active view or routes to the corresponding page.
Toggling the notification switches immediately updates the component state.
Clicking 'Save changes' sends a POST/PATCH request to update the user profile and displays a success toast.
